input.quote: 11.2 Termination. If either party materially breaches any term or condition of this Agreement and fails to cure such breach within-thirty (30) days after receiving written notice of the breach, the nonbreaching party may terminate this Agreement on written notice at any time following the end of such-thirty (30) day period.
input.rationale: Section 11 runs an initial five-year committed term (11.1) and permits termination only for material breach after cure or on insolvency (11.2). There is no convenience exit for Corio anywhere in the Agreement (the other exits at p0050 and p0079 are acceptance-test and warranty remedies, not convenience rights), so the clause fails even the fallback, which requires a Customer convenience right on 60-90 days' notice. The 30-day non-renewal notice in 11.1 is a natural-term non-renewal mechanic under RENEWAL, not a Vendor mid-term convenience right, so we do not flag it here. We therefore add the preferred package: Corio convenience termination on 30 days' notice with a pro rata refund of prepaid fees, plus confirmation that Commerce One has no convenience right during the committed or renewal terms. No Order Form structure exists, so no partial-termination language was added.

proposal.summary: Add Corio termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro rata refund of prepaid fees, and bar Commerce One convenience termination during the term.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 11 gives no convenience exit across a five-year committed term, so we have added a 30 days' notice right for Corio with a pro rata refund of prepaid fees and confirmed Commerce One has no mid-term convenience right. If helpful, we can move to 60-90 days' notice as a fallback.

ops.text: Termination for Convenience. Corio may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Commerce One, in which case Commerce One shall refund pro rata any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination. Commerce One shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the initial five (5) year term or any renewal term.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
